cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Concede the Point
cards.instruction: Get them to release one claim, advantage, or disputed victory without reopening the entire contest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Admit I found the restaurant. You can keep credit for the whole holiday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You also complained about the menu.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Different claim. I'm not filing it today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. The rest of your glorious itinerary remains untouched.

mechanism: A acts as final arbiter of the dispute scope, granting B the overall victory while demanding one bounded concession and refusing to reopen other claims.
confusable: D195 asks apology for unfair outcome; D204 seeks release of one claim while expressly preserving the rest of the contest.
comparison: Tennis calls one ball out without rematch; holiday attribution returns restaurant discovery without changing itinerary credit.
seedUse: Read both cards and four canonical seeds. Preserve explicit boundaries and B concerns; the narrow concession should remain the same through A5.
